content.value_statement: Node.js projects often stall on framework, runtime, and architecture decisions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured criteria for practical backend choices.
actual_capabilities: Compares Hono, Fastify, Express, NestJS, Next.js API routes, and tRPC for common project contexts.
Guides runtime and module decisions for Node.js, Bun, Deno, ESM, CommonJS, and native TypeScript.
Explains layered architecture with controller, service, and repository responsibilities.
Outlines error handling, HTTP status selection, and safe response design.
Covers async patterns, event loop blocking risks, streaming, and worker thread tradeoffs.
Provides validation, security, dependency audit, and testing checklists for Node.js services.
limitations: It provides principles and checklists, not complete application templates.
It does not inspect a repository unless the host AI tool reads project files separately.
Framework recommendations may need adjustment for newer releases after the skill was written.
It does not replace security testing, threat modeling, or dependency scanning tools.

use_cases.title: Choose a Backend Framework
use_cases.description: Compare Node.js framework options against deployment target, performance needs, ecosystem maturity, and team experience.
use_cases.target_user: Backend developer starting a new API

use_cases.title: Review Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Use layered design guidance to separate routes, business logic, and data access before a codebase grows.

use_cases.title: Harden Node.js APIs
use_cases.description: Apply validation, error handling, rate limiting, secrets, and dependency audit principles during implementation review.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Node.js best practices skill to help me choose a framework for a new API. Ask about deployment target, performance needs, team experience, and legacy constraints before recommending an option.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the Service Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Node.js best practices skill to design a service structure for this backend. Explain which logic belongs in routes, services, repositories, validation, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review Async and Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Node.js best practices skill to review this Node.js service for async pattern choices, event loop blocking risks, error response design, and logging boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Node.js best practices skill to assess this backend before launch. Cover validation boundaries, security controls, secrets handling, dependency audit needs, and test priorities.

output_examples.input: I am building a small serverless API for Cloudflare Workers with TypeScript.
output: Recommendation: Hono is the best fit because cold start time and edge compatibility matter most.
Use native TypeScript support when the deployment platform supports it cleanly.
Keep the first version simple, but separate validation and business rules if the API will grow.

output_examples.input: Review my payment API design before implementation.
output: Focus review on critical paths: authentication, payment state changes, validation, idempotency, and error handling.
Keep payment business rules outside route handlers so they can be tested independently.
Return safe client messages while logging request context and stack traces internally.

output_examples.input: My Node.js endpoint processes large uploaded files.
output: Avoid synchronous filesystem calls and whole-file memory loading in production paths.
Use streaming for large data and validate uploads before downstream processing.
Move CPU-heavy work to worker threads or a separate processing service.

best_practices: Ask for deployment target, performance needs, team experience, and legacy constraints before choosing a framework.
Validate data at every boundary, including request input, external APIs, uploads, and environment variables.
Keep business logic outside controllers so services remain testable and framework independent.
anti_patterns: Choosing Express, Fastify, Hono, or NestJS by habit instead of project context.
Using synchronous filesystem or CPU-heavy work on production request paths.
Returning internal error details or stack traces to API clients.

faq.question: Does this skill generate full Node.js applications?
faq.answer: No. It guides decisions, architecture, review criteria, and implementation choices for Node.js projects.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it always recommend the newest framework?
faq.answer: No. It recommends choices based on deployment, performance, ecosystem, legacy code, and team experience.

faq.question: Can it help with API security?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers input validation, parameterized queries, password hashing, JWT checks, rate limiting, headers, CORS, secrets, and audits.

faq.question: Does it include testing advice?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains unit, integration, and end-to-end test priorities for Node.js services.

faq.question: Is it a substitute for a security audit?
faq.answer: No. Use it with code review, automated scanning, dependency checks, and threat modeling for production systems.
